provinces.name: Bangkok
provinces.blurb: The capital and a special administrative area with an elected governor, holding about a tenth of the population and over a third of GDP.

provinces.name: Samut Prakan
provinces.blurb: Bangkok's industrial southern edge, home to Suvarnabhumi Airport and the factories along the Chao Phraya mouth.

provinces.name: Nonthaburi
provinces.blurb: A commuter province north of the capital, now joined to it by the Purple and Pink lines.

provinces.name: Pathum Thani
provinces.blurb: Industrial estates, universities and Rangsit's sprawl, among the worst hit by the 2011 floods.

provinces.name: Ayutthaya
provinces.blurb: The old royal capital, a World Heritage site ringed by Japanese-owned industrial estates.

provinces.name: Ang Thong
provinces.blurb: A small rice province on the Chao Phraya, known for its giant seated Buddha.

provinces.name: Lop Buri
provinces.blurb: Khmer ruins, monkeys and the army's largest garrison town.

provinces.name: Sing Buri
provinces.blurb: One of the smallest provinces, rice country remembered for the Bang Rachan stand against Burma.

provinces.name: Chai Nat
provinces.blurb: Where the Chao Phraya Dam divides the river to irrigate the central plain.

provinces.name: Saraburi
provinces.blurb: Cement plants and limestone quarries on the road from Bangkok to the Northeast.

provinces.name: Chonburi
provinces.blurb: The heart of the Eastern Economic Corridor: Laem Chabang port, Pattaya and the car plants.

provinces.name: Rayong
provinces.blurb: Map Ta Phut's petrochemical complex, the EEC's industrial core and Thailand's highest output per head.

provinces.name: Chanthaburi
provinces.blurb: Durian orchards and the gem trade, with a coast facing Cambodia.

provinces.name: Trat
provinces.blurb: The eastern tip on the Cambodian border, gateway to Ko Chang.

provinces.name: Chachoengsao
provinces.blurb: An EEC province where Bangkok's suburbs meet rice fields and new industrial estates.

provinces.name: Prachin Buri
provinces.blurb: Industrial estates and the Khao Yai forest's eastern edge.

provinces.name: Nakhon Nayok
provinces.blurb: A small province of waterfalls, the army academy and weekend escapes from Bangkok.

provinces.name: Sa Kaeo
provinces.blurb: The main land border with Cambodia, with the Aranyaprathet–Poipet crossing and its casinos.

provinces.name: Nakhon Ratchasima
provinces.blurb: Korat, the largest province by area and the Northeast's gateway, on the high-speed line to Laos.

provinces.name: Buriram
provinces.blurb: Bhumjaithai's home base, with Phanom Rung temple, a MotoGP circuit and a champion football club.

provinces.name: Surin
provinces.blurb: Elephant villages, Khmer-speaking communities and Ta Muen temples on the disputed Cambodian border.

provinces.name: Si Sa Ket
provinces.blurb: A poor rice province facing Preah Vihear across the most contested stretch of the border.

provinces.name: Ubon Ratchathani
provinces.blurb: The Northeast's eastern hub where the Mun meets the Mekong, bordering both Laos and Cambodia.

provinces.name: Yasothon
provinces.blurb: Organic jasmine rice and the rocket festival.

provinces.name: Chaiyaphum
provinces.blurb: Hill country between the Northeast and the central plain, known for silk and sunflowers.

provinces.name: Amnat Charoen
provinces.blurb: A small Mekong-side province carved out of Ubon in 1993.

provinces.name: Bueng Kan
provinces.blurb: The newest province, split from Nong Khai in 2011, rubber country on the Mekong.

provinces.name: Nong Bua Lam Phu
provinces.blurb: A small rural province of the upper Northeast, mostly rice and cassava.

provinces.name: Khon Kaen
provinces.blurb: The Northeast's university and medical centre and a pilot city for smart urban transit.

provinces.name: Udon Thani
provinces.blurb: A trading hub and former US airbase, close to the Laos border and potash deposits.

provinces.name: Loei
provinces.blurb: Mountains, cold winters and gold mining on the Laos border.

provinces.name: Nong Khai
provinces.blurb: The Friendship Bridge to Vientiane and the railhead for the line to China.

provinces.name: Maha Sarakham
provinces.blurb: A university town in the middle of the Northeast's rice belt.

provinces.name: Roi Et
provinces.blurb: A rice province at the centre of the Northeast, its town built around a lake.

provinces.name: Kalasin
provinces.blurb: Dinosaur fossils, silk and the Lam Pao dam.

provinces.name: Sakon Nakhon
provinces.blurb: Forest monasteries, indigo dyeing and Nong Han lake.

provinces.name: Nakhon Phanom
provinces.blurb: A Mekong town facing Laos, with the That Phanom stupa.

provinces.name: Mukdahan
provinces.blurb: The bridge to Savannakhet and the East–West Economic Corridor to Vietnam.

provinces.name: Chiang Mai
provinces.blurb: The North's capital, a tourism and digital-nomad hub at the foot of Doi Suthep.

provinces.name: Lamphun
provinces.blurb: The oldest city in the North and its main industrial estate for electronics.

provinces.name: Lampang
provinces.blurb: Horse carriages, ceramics and the Mae Moh lignite power plant.

provinces.name: Uttaradit
provinces.blurb: Hill country between the North and the central plain, at the Sirikit Dam.

provinces.name: Phrae
provinces.blurb: Teak houses and a quiet northern town on the new Den Chai–Chiang Khong railway.

provinces.name: Nan
provinces.blurb: A remote mountain province on the Laos border, fighting deforestation from corn farming.

provinces.name: Phayao
provinces.blurb: A northern province built around Kwan Phayao, a large shallow lake.

provinces.name: Chiang Rai
provinces.blurb: The Golden Triangle, the White Temple and the road and river trade with Myanmar, Laos and China.

provinces.name: Mae Hong Son
provinces.blurb: Remote, forested and mountainous, bordering Myanmar's Shan State.

provinces.name: Nakhon Sawan
provinces.blurb: Where the Ping and Nan rivers form the Chao Phraya, a rice and sugar hub.

provinces.name: Uthai Thani
provinces.blurb: A quiet province on the edge of the Huai Kha Khaeng wildlife sanctuary.

provinces.name: Kamphaeng Phet
provinces.blurb: Sukhothai-era ruins and a big cassava and sugarcane belt.

provinces.name: Tak
provinces.blurb: Mae Sot's border trade with Myanmar, factories staffed by migrants and refugee camps in the hills.

provinces.name: Sukhothai
provinces.blurb: The first Thai capital, now a World Heritage park.

provinces.name: Phitsanulok
provinces.blurb: A rail and road junction for the lower North, birthplace of King Naresuan.

provinces.name: Phichit
provinces.blurb: Low-lying rice farms on the Nan river.

provinces.name: Phetchabun
provinces.blurb: Mountain resorts and corn country between the North and the Northeast.

provinces.name: Ratchaburi
provinces.blurb: Floating markets, ceramics and power plants west of Bangkok.

provinces.name: Kanchanaburi
provinces.blurb: The Death Railway bridge, dams and the forests along the Myanmar border.

provinces.name: Suphan Buri
provinces.blurb: A rice province whose road network shows decades of patronage politics.

provinces.name: Nakhon Pathom
provinces.blurb: Home of Phra Pathom Chedi, the tallest stupa, and of Bangkok's western suburbs.

provinces.name: Samut Sakhon
provinces.blurb: Seafood processing staffed largely by migrant workers from Myanmar.

provinces.name: Samut Songkhram
provinces.blurb: The smallest province, with salt flats and the Mae Klong railway market.

provinces.name: Phetchaburi
provinces.blurb: Palaces, palm sugar and the beaches of Cha-am.

provinces.name: Prachuap Khiri Khan
provinces.blurb: Hua Hin, pineapples and the narrowest part of the country.

provinces.name: Nakhon Si Thammarat
provinces.blurb: The South's historic religious centre and its largest province by population.

provinces.name: Krabi
provinces.blurb: Limestone islands and beaches on the Andaman, one of tourism's big earners.

provinces.name: Phangnga
provinces.blurb: Phang Nga Bay's karst islands, hit hardest by the 2004 tsunami.

provinces.name: Phuket
provinces.blurb: The largest island and a tourism economy that earns more per head than almost anywhere outside Bangkok.

provinces.name: Surat Thani
provinces.blurb: Rubber, palm oil and the ferries to Ko Samui.

provinces.name: Ranong
provinces.blurb: The wettest province, facing Myanmar across the Kraburi river and the Land Bridge's western end.

provinces.name: Chumphon
provinces.blurb: The narrow Kra Isthmus and the Land Bridge's eastern end.

provinces.name: Songkhla
provinces.blurb: Hat Yai's trade with Malaysia and the South's main port and university.

provinces.name: Satun
provinces.blurb: A quiet Muslim-majority province on the Andaman with a UNESCO geopark.

provinces.name: Trang
provinces.blurb: Rubber plantations and island-hopping on the Andaman coast.

provinces.name: Phatthalung
provinces.blurb: Rice fields and wetlands on the shore of Songkhla Lake.

provinces.name: Pattani
provinces.blurb: Once the seat of a Malay sultanate, now at the centre of the southern insurgency.

provinces.name: Yala
provinces.blurb: The southernmost inland province, under emergency rule since 2005.

provinces.name: Narathiwat
provinces.blurb: The far south on the Malaysian border, Malay-speaking and under emergency rule.
